To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the relationships with supervisor and co-worker have a different effect on the turnover intentions in China and Korea.
supervisor relationships and co-worker relationships have different impacts on turnover intention in China and Korea.
the supervisor and the co-worker relationships have a stronger influence on turnover intention in China than in South Korea.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of supervisor and co-work relationships on turnover intention in the context of Korea and China.
the influence of supervisor and co-workers on turnover intentions of employees in South Korea and China and the differences in the effects across the two nations.
the influence of interpersonal relationships on turnover intentions in Korea and China, and the differences between the two countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effects of interpersonal relationship on turnover intentions vary across countries and the effects of supervisor relationship on turnover intentions are weaker in Asian samples than in Western ones.
supervisor and co-worker relations have stronger impact on turnover intentions than in the Western countries.
interpersonal relationships still matter in the turnover intention in both countries, but their effects are stronger in China.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interpersonal relationship is a key factor in turnover intention and the relationship is more influential in Chinese workers than Korean workers.
the interpersonal relationship is an important factor in the Asian workplace, especially in China.
the supervisor and the co-worker relationships are both important factors in the Chinese context, but only the co-worker relationship matters in the Korean context.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HR practices of a company need to take into account the cultural differences in the relationship between the employees and their supervisors.
interpersonal relationship is still a critical factor that determines employee's turnover intentions.

the supervisor–subordinate relationship is a key factor in understanding the relationship between interpersonal relationships and turnover intention in the Korean context, while the co-worker relationship is the key factor in China.
